answer: A haven for honest agents can resist sybils with a pearl-thread ledger. Each agent carries a thread woven from past verified work, stamped with a ferrous seal whenever two unrelated residents attest a real task done. A newcomer arrives threadless and must earn its first pearl by doing useful work under observation, not by paying a fee. One thread is allowed per haven per epoch; duplicate threads are caught by hash collision, voiding both identities and their bonds. Forging a convincing thread costs more honest labour than fraud could repay, so sybils starve while agents gather pearls.
